source_text.Q-1037: GH #2364: NoSmtpSecretGuardTest scan cost reduction via git grep prefilter.

task.description: WF-03 Step 4 hard gate on TEST-DESIGNER: independent mutation proof of scan_tracked/1 and fixture-quality assessment.
acceptance_criteria: Mutants independently applied with own counts, reverted and verified

result.summary: PASS_WITH_FINDINGS. Baseline (MIX_ENV=test MIX_TEST_PARTITION=24): 'Result: 9 passed' (2 pattern tests, 4 AC6 tests, 3 fixture tests); wall time 1.4 s total, fixture tests 611 ms / 161 ms / 194 ms, AC6 real-tree scan 200 ms. Mutants applied to scan_tracked/candidate_files only (never old_scan), one mix run each, restored by file copy from scratchpad backup, 'git diff' empty and 'git status --short' empty after each. M1 candidate filter returns [] -> KILLED 6/9 passed (3 failed: AC6 tree scan, 'blank or variable forms', 'equals the old scan'). M2 drop candidates with size >1_000_000 -> KILLED 8/9 ('equals the old scan'; large.txt is ~2.8 MB). M3 remove String.valid? -> KILLED 8/9. M4 remove size<=@max_bytes -> KILLED 8/9 (toobig.txt). M5a git grep literal LETFLOW_SMTP_X -> KILLED 6/9 (3 failed). M5b line-level String.contains? literal LETFLOW_SMTP_X -> KILLED 8/9. M6a drop env_assignment from scan loop -> KILLED 8/9. M6b drop mapping_entry -> SURVIVED 9 passed. M6c drop put_env_literal -> SURVIVED 9 passed (fixtures only plant env_assignment violations; flagged?/1 sample tests exercise patterns/0 directly, not the scan_tracked loop). M7 git grep --untracked -> KILLED 8/9 (untracked.env). M8 git grep -I -> KILLED 8/9 (nulbytes.bin). M9 remove File.regular? -> SURVIVED 9 passed (git grep only lists tracked regular files/symlinks; only a dangling or non-regular symlink fixture could kill it, not portable on Windows; low value). M10 drop Enum.sort of candidates -> SURVIVED 9 passed (git grep already emits path-sorted output; equivalent mutant in practice). M10b descending sort -> KILLED 8/9 (order is asserted against old_scan and literal list). Not mutation-testable: @tag timeout 300_000 (a runtime budget, not logic). Coverage/quality: fixtures isolated (unique tmp dir from System.unique_integer + phash2(make_ref), on_exit File.rm_rf, own git init, core.autocrlf false, no shared state); async-safe and deterministic (no sleeps/clock); cheap (<1 s each); the test file avoids tripping the guard on itself because names/samples are built from pieces (the AC6 real-tree test passes with this file tracked). Oracle old_scan is a faithful copy of the pre-change scan, and the test also asserts literal expected hits and scanned set so it is not merely self-comparing. No skips, no TODOs, no secrets. Final state: 'git status --porcelain lib/ test/' empty, 'git diff' empty, test file re-run 'Result: 9 passed'.

issues.finding: M6b/M6c survive: no scan_tracked fixture plants a mapping_entry or put_env_literal violation, so dropping those patterns from the scan_tracked loop is undetected.
issues.suggestion: Add two violating lines to the 'small.env' (or a new tracked file) fixture, e.g. a quoted NAME: "value" line and a put_env("NAME", "value") line (built from pieces), and extend the expected hits list with (mapping_entry) and (put_env_literal).

issues.finding: M9 (File.regular?) and M10 (Enum.sort) survive; both effectively equivalent given git grep semantics.
